text: Knowing a vendor's risk is yours doesn't help until you can actually assess it. This lesson is about turning "we trust this vendor" into a real, repeatable process, using tools the industry has already standardized instead of reinventing a questionnaire from scratch every time.

Two standardized questionnaires solve the reinvention problem. SIG, maintained by Shared Assessments, is a comprehensive, modular questionnaire covering governance, access control, data handling, and incident response, with a shorter SIG Lite for lower-risk engagements. CAIQ, from the Cloud Security Alliance, is built specifically for cloud providers and maps directly to the CSA's Cloud Controls Matrix, so a yes answer points to a named, published control. Either one beats a custom form: answers become comparable across vendors, and vendors can reuse work they've already done for other customers.

The single most expensive mistake in this field is treating every vendor identically — the same full questionnaire and review cycle for a cloud provider holding regulated data and for an office supplier. That burns the GRC team's time on low-risk vendors while a genuinely high-risk one gets the same rubber stamp as everyone else.

Real programs tier vendors first, along two axes: data sensitivity, whether a vendor touches regulated or confidential data, and access level, whether it has network, system, or physical access to your environment. High on both axes — a payroll processor with a direct system integration — lands in Tier 1: full SIG, a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 report review, and the contractual protections Lesson 23 covers. Low on both gets a light intake questionnaire and nothing more.

A questionnaire answer is still self-reported — the vendor grading its own homework. The highest-risk tiers need independent evidence backing it up: a current SOC 2 Type II report, an ISO 27001 certificate with its Statement of Applicability, or a recent penetration test summary. A vendor that answers every question perfectly but can't produce any of that evidence is itself a finding worth escalating.

Tiered, evidence-backed assessment means the vendors that matter most get real scrutiny, without drowning the GRC team in full reviews for vendors that pose almost no risk at all. None of this is a one-time gate, though — Lesson 24 covers why a vendor that passed cleanly last year can look very different today.
